rulings.model: IRS line 10 says 'Was your annuity starting date before 1987? Yes. STOP Do not complete the rest of this worksheet'; the restatement adds line 6 and line 8 even for a pre-1987 annuity.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi (2025) p.29 worksheet lines5/10 give skip/STOP rules for annuities beginning before1987. retirement.special excludes every after-tax-cost annuity starting before November19,1996, and retirement.taxable/amount_a enforce that screen; the positive annuity interface also requires a later start. Hence no supported completed Simplified Method case reaches the pre1987 regime. Retain the later-start computation; this does not claim the standalone worksheet values match an excluded old annuity or that the IRS skip is absent.

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from helper "Your cost in the plan at the annuity starting date (Simplified Method Worksheet, line 2)".
rulings.model: The worksheet's before-you-begin note says to 'include any death benefit exclusion that you are entitled to (up to $5,000) in the amount entered on line 2'; the restatement uses only the cost helper and omits that addition.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi (2025) p.29 worksheet preamble includes any entitled death-benefit exclusion in line2. The retirement.special question expressly screens a death-benefit exclusion; retirement.taxable and retirement.amount_a refuse it, as does retirement.rolled. A supported completed distribution therefore has no such addition and uses after-tax cost. The broader source case is excluded, not model noise; no standalone correctness claim is made on an excluded distribution.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Did you complete this worksheet for this annuity last year?" = true → helper "Line 4 of last year's Simplified Method Worksheet"] [helper "Did you complete this worksheet for this annuity last year?" = false → helper "Line 2 divided by the number on line 3 (Table 2 for a joint and survivor annuity starting after 1997, Table 1 otherwise)"]
rulings.model: The Table 1 helper uses only the after-November 18-1996 numbers; IRS Table 1 also has a before-November 19-1996 column, so a pre-November 19, 1996 annuity would use 300/260/240/170/120 rather than 360/310/260/210/160.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi (2025) p.29 Table1 includes an older-annuity column. retirement.special expressly screens an after-tax-cost annuity starting before November19,1996, and retirement.annuity asks whether the start is after November18,1996; retirement.taxable/amount_a refuse the excluded case. Supported Simplified Method distributions therefore use the later column. The missing older column is a documented scope reduction, not an error in that IRS column.
